# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 48 (Bu-Vb Sk48)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk48
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 48
**Title (English, from literature):** Scattering rice

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sitthāvakāraka Sikkhāpada* (“Scattering rice,” Sekhiya 48) is a training rule for Buddhist monastics located in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule belongs to the *sekhiya* section of the monastic code, which sets out standards of proper deportment and table manners, specifically instructing monastics not to drop or scatter particles of rice while eating. A modern English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In the Pali Vinaya, exact counterparts exist in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sk 48), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha (Sk 48), and the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Sk 48). Parallels in other Vinaya lineages are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit across multiple early schools, including the Sarvāstivāda (e.g., Chinese Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sk 77; Sanskrit Prātimokṣa Sk 80, Sk 81), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese Sk 58; Sanskrit Sk 58, Sk 59), Mahīśāsaka (Chinese Sk 59), Dharmaguptaka (Chinese Sk 40), Mahāsāṅghika (Chinese Sk 40; Sanskrit Sk 42), and Lokottaravāda (Sanskrit Bhikkhu Prātimokṣa Sk 42, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sk 43).
